title.narrative: Support services for Survivor Bangladeshi Returnee Migrant Workers 2025-2026

description.narrative:
This grant will cover a sudden funding gap in OKUP's budget caused by USAID funding cuts and will be fully covered by CPL Aromas. The project provides comprehensive services to returnee migrant workers, including safe shelter, health and psychosocial support, legal aid, life skills training and vocational training, and livelihood assistance etc. By ensuring access to essential services, the project helps survivors regain stability, rebuild their lives, and reintegrate into society with dignity. It also provides Pre-Departure Orientation sessions for final stage outbound migrants workers, with the main goal of equipping them with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the challenges of working abroad, ensuring a smoother transition and a more positive experience.
Migrant workers play a significant role in the socioeconomic development of both Bangladesh and the countries of destination. It is the 8th largest labour sending country in the world with an annual average of 340,000 people migrating of whom 9% are women. Remittances sent by Bangladeshi migrant workers constitute one of the country’s largest sources of foreign exchange earnings, driving economic stability and development. However, despite their indispensable role, migrant workers frequently face unethical recruitment practices, exploitation, violations of rights, and significant barriers in accessing justice, both in Bangladesh and abroad. OKUP works to raise awareness amongst migrants of their rights pre-departure; support returnee migrants who have suffered abuse when they return socially and economically; and advocate for improvements to the Bangladeshi legal system so that survivors can obtain justice and compensation.
